routes.reason: No layer plans functional transcendence for Shimura varieties, jet spaces, Hermitian Schwarzians or differential Ax–Schanuel; the atlas search terms ('weakly special', 'bi-algebraic', 'Schwarzian', 'jet space', 'differential field', 'Hwang', 'Ochiai', 'Seidenberg') return nothing relevant. LD.6's source route names Ax–Lindemann/Ax–Schanuel inputs, so a Part II in LD.6's direction is right. The title matches the parent's, and the area modeltheory is a galaxy id. Accepted after amendments in place: item 2 moved here from the rejected D4 route, items 41–44 added, imports corrected (AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3 for Siegel sets, ComplexComparisonPartII C0 and C4), and a design constraint added to import only LD.6's o-minimality and counting content, because LD.6's applications consume this Part II. Coordination: PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 (review pending) routes weakly special subvarieties to LD.6; one owner should be chosen at design time, and this Part II is the natural one.

Definable Remmert–Stein and definable Chow (Peterzil–Starchenko) are o-minimal theorems with no Shimura content, and every consumer of LD.6's o-minimality needs them. LD.6 is the right layer; the blueprint will also import Chow's theorem from ComplexComparisonPartII C4. This is compatible with PAPER-BAKKER-KLINGLER-TSIMERMAN-20's source route of o-minimal inputs to LD.0 and LD.6.

Added by this review for item 40. The semicontinuity of fibre dimension and Remmert's proper mapping theorem are classical complex analytic geometry that no layer plans. ComplexComparisonPartII C0 (closed analytic subspaces) and C4 (Chow algebraization via a proper projection) are their owners, as PAPER-BAKKER-KLINGLER-TSIMERMAN-20 also proposes for its proper-image theorem.
